text:
helen: Quick PSA — I pulled the access-recert dashboard and there's a backlog: ~420 entities waiting review across prod projects. Some have stale admin flags dating back >180 days.
sec-bot: Automated report: recert-backlog-2026-03-22.csv uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-sec/reports/recert-backlog-4312345678.csv) :file_folder:
jay: Yikes. Do we have an owner coverage metric? who is responsible for the old admin roles?
helen: Ownership OOO in many cases — roughly 60% of items show no owner tag. I sampled 20 and 4 were service accounts with admin=true that haven't had usage in 90d.
kim: Any link to the KMS bindings? last time we removed admin bits we hit a key-without-grants incident.
helen: Link: https://console.redwood.internal/sec/recert/4312345678. The CSV has a KMS column; several keys lack the project tag. I flagged those as HIGH for manual review.
jay: For the service accounts, can we run a dry-run that simulates privilege removal and then run integration smoke tests? If tests fail we roll back.
matt: +1 on dry-run. Also we need a clear rollback playbook. If we pull admin from a SA that is used in CI, we need a quick way to rebind.
helen: Proposed plan:
- Phase A (this week): triage backlog, add owner tags where known, and create exception tickets for any infra-critical items.
- Phase B (next week): run a non-destructive dry-run script that reports ACL impact (no writes).
- Phase C (two weeks): scheduled low-risk remediation window with oncall standby.
kim: What's the dry-run command? can you share snippet?
helen: Snippet:
```
# dry-run remove admin flag (no change)
python infra/tools/acl_check.py --project $PROJECT --role admin --simulate
```
It outputs impacted principals and affected resources.
jay: For KMS: we should cross-check keys where the SA principal appears in key policy/grants. Quick gcloud check:
```
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy KEY --location=global --keyring=KR --format=json
```
Look for principals matching serviceAccount:...@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
matt: IR angle: if we detect an unexpected failure after removal, escalation path:
1) page infra-oncall
2) rebind removed roles via emergency script (kept in vault, audited)
3) notify affected teams & rollback tickets
Make sure the emergency script is accessible only to SRE-leads and sec-admins.
sec-bot: Note: emergency-bind-script last run 2025-11-09; access logs show two uses. Audit trail stored in vault://audits/emerbind/4312345678
helen: Action items:
- @jay: collect smoke-test matrix for CI consumers (due EOD Thu)
- @kim: run KMS-grant cross-check and list keys w/o project tags (due Fri)
- @matt: review emergency rollback script permissions & update playbook (due Mon)
- @helen: run Phase A triage and attach owner tags where possible (start now)
jay: I'll ping the CI teams for quick test windows. Also propose a 48h notification window before any role removals.
kim: If we find keys missing tags, suggest adding a tag enforcement job in infra (low-effort): tag missing => ticket to owner.
matt: Agree. Also let's record a short postmortem template if anything goes wrong during the window.
helen: OK will create a board ticket and schedule the dry-run. Keeping this thread for status updates — please drop short updates here.
jay: Update: CI owners pinged, awaiting responses from payments + search teams.
kim: KMS cross-check done, attached CSV in the board ticket — 9 keys missing project tag, 2 of those used by cron SAs (flagged HIGH).
matt: Emergency script perms reviewed; locked to sres + sec-leads, will rotate keys after verification.
helen: Thanks all. Next status: I'll post Phase A summary in 24h. :thumbsup:
